subject: Acme Systems — Renewal & Expansion recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Priya Sharma <pri.sha@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Systems — Renewal & Expansion recap and next steps

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we covered and the proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of current usage and ask: 
- Current footprint: ~12k requests/day, majority inference for chat assistant (medium latency requirement, 95th percentile ~350ms).
- Pain points: unpredictable token costs on peak days, increased latency under batch workloads, and early concerns about PII scrubbing for customer transcripts.
- Goal: Renew current contract and add a second pool for R&D / higher-throughput batch workloads to reduce tail latency and get better unit economics.

Proposed expansion path: 
1) Dedicated GPU pool for batch inference (initially 2x V100-equivalent nodes) to handle nightly workloads — expected 30% cost reduction for batch tokens.
2) Model/config recommendations (quantized variant + prefix caching) for chat path to improve 95th percentile latency.
3) Optional add-on: PII scrubber pipeline + on-premise KMS integration for regulated workflows (requires security review).

Action items / timeline we agreed on: 
- I will send a Mutual Action Plan (attached) with milestones and target dates — target renewal signature by 2027-05-20. [Attachment: Acme_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
- Neha will follow up with a short technical note on quantization and expected perf gains by 2027-04-13.
- Jordan / Priya to confirm internal stakeholder list for procurement + any required legal security docs by 2027-04-18.

Attached I’ve included the mutual action plan and the updated pricing options for Q2 (high-level). I’ve also linked the HubSpot deal for tracking.

If that looks right, we’ll draft the renewal quote (with the expansion seat) and route for signature next week.

Thanks — appreciate the partnership.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Acme_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: Redwood_PRICING_Q2_2027.pdf (pdf)]

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Systems — Renewal & Expansion recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful and matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) For the batch pool, can you confirm whether the pricing in the attached PDF assumes preemptible instances or reserved capacity? We’re leaning towards reserved for predictability.
2) For PII scrubbing, our legal team will need a short architecture note (what runs where, whether transcripts leave our VPC). Can Neha send that by EOD Wednesday?

Also looping in Priya — she’ll own procurement. Priya, if you can confirm next steps for the vendor review and internal approvers that would be great.

On the timeline: target of 2027-05-20 works, but we may need to move signatures earlier if procurement wants extra review time.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>, Priya Sharma <pri.sha@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Systems — Renewal & Expansion recap and next steps

Jordan / Priya —

Quick technical notes as promised: 
- Reserved capacity assumption: the pricing doc attached to Marissa’s note models reserved capacity (monthly commit) for the dedicated batch pool. We can provide a burst-to-hosted option if you want ondemand bumping.
- Quantization + prefix caching: for your chat workload, moving to an int8 quantized model variant + prefix/KV cache will reduce CPU/GPU cycles and lower token costs ~20-35% depending on sequence length distribution. Expected 95th p latency improvement of 40-80ms in our testing for your median sequence lengths.
- PII scrubber architecture: recommended pattern is client-side tokenization + on-host pipeline that scrubs sensitive entities before anything leaves your VPC. If you prefer, we can offer an isolated on-prem variant. I’ve attached a one-page architecture note.

Next steps from our side: 
- I’ll upload the short architecture note and a perf table by EOD today. [Attachment: PII_Scrubber_Architecture.pdf]
- Marissa — I’ll sync with you on the exact node sizing after we get a sample of your batch job size distribution.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

[Attachment: PII_Scrubber_Architecture.pdf (pdf)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Acme procurement / internal next steps (internal)

Marissa / Neha —

Thanks — looping internally to confirm procurement cadence. A few internal items I’ll own / we should prepare: 
- Draft SOW and renewal quote (including the dedicated batch pool line items) — I’ll start the SOW draft today and will use the pricing PDF as the basis.
- Support plan addendum (4x9 vs 24x7 options) — please list recommended support tier for this expansion.
- Security artifacts: we need to prepare a short packet (SOC 2 summary, PII scrubber arch note, KMS options) to hand to Acme legal. Neha’s architecture note will slot into that packet.

Target: aim to have the SOW + support addendum ready for internal review by 2027-04-22 so Marissa can share with Acme and keep the 2027-05-20 signature target.

I’ll update the HubSpot deal and create the DocuSign envelope once Marissa confirms final numbers.

-Rishi
